offers: Thirteen other Czech studios on the same stand

area-35-business.description: The publisher on its trade stand, taking submissions and distribution meetings. Its games are playable in Hall 10.1.
area-35-business.accessNote: 61 m², open — a stand you can walk up to in the Hall 2.2 row.

4divinity.description: GCL's publishing arm, showing six titles across three stands: the main one in Hall 7.1, a second in Hall 6.1 and a business booth in Hall 4.2. The lineup spans a World War II shooter (The Defiant), NEKCOM's retro-Americana RPG Showa American Story, the occult-western Guns of Eschaton and three Chinese-mythology action RPGs. Which titles are hands-on rather than trailer-only has not been broken down.
4divinity.crowdNote: A large Hall 7.1 stand beside Xbox, but a lineup still new to Western audiences — busy without AAA-scale queues.
4divinity.visitAdvice: The two stands show different games: Showa American Story and The Defiant in Hall 6.1, Guns of Eschaton in Hall 7.1. Check which one you actually want before walking over.

games.The Defiant: AAA World War II shooter from Hoothanes; shown at the Hall 6.1 stand.
games.Showa American Story: NEKCOM's retro pop-culture RPG; shown at the Hall 6.1 stand.
games.Guns of Eschaton: Occult-western soulslike shooter from Eschatology Entertainment; shown at the Hall 7.1 stand.
games.A Whisper of Fall: Jinyiwei: Ming-dynasty action RPG from CangMo Game Entertainment.
games.Genigods: Nezha: Chinese-mythology action RPG from Genigods Lab — also on Xbox's Hall 7.1 stand.
games.Sword Sage: Awakening: Myth-driven action RPG from Sword Panda.

secret-mode.description: Sumo Group's publishing label takes a Hall 6.1 stand at B040. Its gamescom entry files it under racing games and lists no titles, and nothing has been announced for the booth.
secret-mode.crowdNote: A small stand for an indie-scale publisher — walk-up.
secret-mode.visitAdvice: Nothing announced yet, so treat it as something to glance at while passing B040 rather than a planned stop.

pawprint-aniimo.description: Singapore's Pawprint Interactive at Hall 6.1 C041, registered under its game's own brand: Aniimo, an open-world creature-collecting RPG for PC, console and mobile.
pawprint-aniimo.crowdNote: Creature-collectors draw steady interest and this is a mid-size stand — expect a short rotating line.
pawprint-aniimo.visitAdvice: Sits in the same Hall 6.1 aisle as Elementa Games and Secret Mode, so the three make one short detour off the publisher row.

games.Aniimo: Open-world creature-collecting RPG; the booth is registered under this brand rather than the studio name.

elementa-games.description: Singapore developer Elementa, with a Hall 6.1 stand at C021 and a business booth in Hall 2.2. Trade press lists Silver Palace for the show; the gamescom entry files the studio under action/adventure and role-playing and names no titles.
elementa-games.crowdNote: Small stand with an all-but-unannounced lineup — low queues.
elementa-games.visitAdvice: A discovery stop rather than a planned one.

huawei-appgallery.description: Aspiegel SE — Huawei's European entity — running AppGallery and its GameCenter at Hall 7.1 B031. A mobile-platform stand rather than a games booth: it is filed under app stores, platforms and mobile phones.
huawei-appgallery.crowdNote: Platform stand: browse-through, no demo queues.
huawei-appgallery.visitAdvice: A two-minute stop between Xbox and Konami if mobile storefronts are of interest.

webedia-fyng-city.description: FYNG City, the games-media village Webedia builds in Hall 7.1: over 1,500 m² across several stand blocks, with the GameStar and MeinMMO editorial teams on site and Mercedes-Benz as main partner. Webedia's registered brands here include GameStar, GamePro, MeinMMO, Moviepilot and Filmstarts.
webedia-fyng-city.crowdNote: A hangout area rather than a demo queue — busy but flowing.
webedia-fyng-city.visitAdvice: One of the few places in Hall 7 to sit down mid-hall. AMD's stand shares the same block at B041/C040.

mbc-game-studio.description: A large Hall 8.1 stand — roughly 610 m² at A011/B010, at the far end of the hall next to Square Enix — plus a business booth in Hall 2.1, for the British-Saudi studio, registered under the brand 'MGS'. Neither gamescom's listing nor the trade press names a game for it yet.
mbc-game-studio.crowdNote: The booth size implies a real presence, but with no announced lineup the draw is unknown.
mbc-game-studio.visitAdvice: Worth a look on your first pass down Hall 8.1 — it is one of the hall's bigger unknowns.

the-district.description: New for 2026: a competitive-gaming area of about 2,000 m² in Hall 8.1 plus roughly 1,000 m² in the reactivated outdoor area P8 behind the hall, with an esports stage at the back of the hall. Cologne's SK Gaming is the headline partner; REWE, Techniker Krankenkasse, Nestlé, Logitech, Deutsche Telekom, Philips, SanDisk, Subway and Esports Virtual Arenas are among the brands on the shared stand and around it.
the-district.crowdNote: Stage-driven: quiet between sessions, packed while a tournament runs.
the-district.visitAdvice: Come for a scheduled session rather than wandering in. The P8 outdoor half is straight out the back of Hall 8 and also holds CD Projekt Red's Apollo Tent, the Red Bull bar and the gamescom Beach.

games.Clutch: Maverick Games' open-world driving game, hands-on all five days in the P8 outdoor half.
games.Star Wars Galactic Racer: Listed at HP/HyperX in the P8 outdoor half in the trade-press games list; no detail published.
games.EA Sports FC 27: Red Bull runs an FC 27 tournament at its booth in the P8 outdoor area — separate from EA's own Hall 6.1 stand.

gigabyte-aorus.description: GIGABYTE and its AORUS gaming brand at Hall 8.1 C050: graphics cards, monitors, laptops and peripherals, registered across components, displays and VR.
gigabyte-aorus.visitAdvice: Part of the same Hall 8.1 hardware run as ASUS ROG, AGON by AOC and Logitech.

mattel.description: Mattel on two stands — Hall 8.1 B020, directly behind Square Enix, and one in the Hall 5.1 merchandise area — for Hot Wheels, Masters of the Universe, UNO and the Mattel Brick Shop.
mattel.crowdNote: Family-facing brand stand; busiest at the weekend.
mattel.visitAdvice: Pair it with the Hall 5 merchandise area if you are shopping rather than demoing.

jbl-quantum.description: Harman's JBL and JBL Quantum gaming-audio line at Hall 9.1 B034/C035 — headsets, headphones and speakers to try on.
jbl-quantum.crowdNote: Small listening stand, no real queue.
jbl-quantum.visitAdvice: Two minutes off the Nintendo-to-Capcom walk through Hall 9.1.

rocket-beans.description: Rocket Beans TV broadcasts the whole show from Hall 9.1 A046/B047 — filed under BEANS Entertainment GmbH — and runs a second stage at the Capcom stand daily from 11:30, including the new BEANSCOMPETITION at 17:00. Live from Tuesday evening through Sunday, with a separate merch stand in Hall 5.2.
rocket-beans.crowdNote: German-language streaming audience: crowds gather for the scheduled formats and thin out between them.
rocket-beans.visitAdvice: Come for a specific slot. The Capcom-stand programme covers Onimusha: Way of the Sword, Dragon's Dogma 2, Mega Man: Dual Override, Street Fighter 6 and Pragmata.

gamescom-merch.description: The official gamescom merchandise shops, run by Campus Sportswear under the gamescomwear brand. The main shops are in the Hall 5.2 merchandise area, with smaller counters in Halls 6.1, 7.1, 8.1, 9.1, 10.1 and 10.2 — which is what those unnamed kiosks along the entertainment-hall aisles are.
gamescom-merch.crowdNote: The Hall 5.2 shops build queues; the in-hall counters stay short.
gamescom-merch.visitAdvice: Use whichever counter is in the hall you are already in rather than walking to Hall 5.2 for it.
